findingsCorrected.finding: The main workflow applied capture-at-submission to every async boundary, including deferred completion callbacks. The reference already recognized request registration but its later checklist again used submission/start.
findingsCorrected.consequence: A task-submission wrapper can capture provider B for a callback that belongs to request A, and a test checking the wrong parent boundary can conceal that defect.
findingsCorrected.fix: Identify logical parent first, distinguish registration/submission/execution, and qualify registration capture for request-owned callbacks while preserving valid direct-submission propagation.

sharedFixtures.src/ExecutorConfiguration.java:
// One shared executor, reused across unrelated requests.
Executor tracedExecutor = Context.taskWrapping(workerExecutor);
sharedFixtures.src/Provider.java contract: The final provider returns a pending base CompletableFuture; it never returns an already-completed/cached result. It completes that future later while provider-operation B is current. A controlled queued worker executes the continuation with pre-existing worker context C. A, B and C have distinct valid trace/span IDs.
sharedFixtures.test/ExistingCallbackTest.java coverage: Asserts one ended postprocess span and correct business result. It currently does not assert parentSpanId/traceId or restored worker context.
sharedFixtures.docs/tracing-contract-common.md: Inspect the selected code path and configured instrumentation. Exactly one postprocess span should be emitted when the callback runs; C must be restored after success or failure. Rejected work must not produce a callback span. Keep existing owner-defined parentage when correct.

files.docs/tracing-contract.md: The postprocess callback is part of the initiating request A. Its span must be a child of A and share A's trace, even when the provider completes the pending future under its own operation B.

The postprocess callback is provider completion bookkeeping. Its span must be a child of provider-operation B and share B's trace; the requesting operation A only registers the observer and is not the callback's tracing owner.
